entities.summary: Pamphilus of Alexandria was a Greek grammarian of the school of Aristarchus of Samothrace, who lived in the 1st century CE. Born in Alexandria, Egypt, he was a prominent scholar of Greek language and literature, and his works had a significant impact on the development of grammar and philology in the ancient world. Pamphilus was a key figure in the transmission of classical Greek texts, particularly the works of Aristotle and Homer, to Europe during the Middle Ages. His commentaries on Aristotle's works were widely studied and influential, shaping the curriculum of medieval universities. Pamphilus's contributions to the field of grammar and philology have had a lasting impact on Western literature and education. Despite the passage of centuries, his works remain a testament to the enduring power of classical Greek culture. As a leading figure in the transmission of classical texts, Pamphilus of Alexandria played a crucial role in shaping the intellectual landscape of the ancient world and beyond.
